capabilities.name: SIEM alert bidirectional updates
capabilities.description: Can the product receive alert changes from the SIEM and write updates back? Specify which fields sync in each direction, such as status, verdict, severity, notes, and reopened alerts. Closing an alert alone is only partial support.

capabilities.name: Responder notifications and escalation
capabilities.description: How does the product notify the right responder when a case needs attention or approval? Identify the supported channels, routing rules, and escalation options.

capabilities.name: Slack and Teams case collaboration
capabilities.description: Can analysts review cases, add context, and approve or reject actions in Slack or Teams? Distinguish two-way case interaction from one-way notifications.

capabilities.name: Platform and integration health dashboards
capabilities.description: Can customers see connector health, processing delays, failed workflows, and platform usage? Explain which dashboards ship with the product and which customers must build.

capabilities.name: Case activity and approval audit trail
capabilities.description: Can a customer reconstruct a case from its inputs, queries, decisions, approvals, and actions? Explain what is recorded, how long it is retained, and whether it can be exported.

capabilities.name: Incident response performance metrics
capabilities.description: Which response metrics can customers track over time, such as time to triage, investigate, and contain? Explain the definitions, reporting filters, and export options.

capabilities.name: Platform activity and error logs
capabilities.description: Can customers access and export logs of user activity, API calls, connector failures, and workflow errors? Explain the search, retention, and troubleshooting options.

capabilities.name: Analyst interface and everyday workflows
capabilities.description: Can analysts review evidence, investigate cases, and manage response actions through the interface? Identify routine tasks that still require code, APIs, or vendor assistance.

capabilities.name: Single sign-on and user account management
capabilities.description: Which identity providers and single sign-on methods are supported? Explain how customers provision users, remove access, and enforce their authentication policies.

capabilities.name: Vendor support coverage and response times
capabilities.description: What support is included, during which hours, and with what response commitments? Identify the escalation process and any support that requires a higher subscription.

capabilities.name: Analyst feedback collection and improvement
capabilities.description: How are analyst corrections and case feedback collected and used to improve the product? Distinguish manual feedback, automatic learning, and changes that require customer approval.

capabilities.name: Auto-closed case review and reversal reporting
capabilities.description: Can customers review cases closed automatically and track those later reopened or overturned? Explain whether review reports are scheduled, how reversals are recorded, and how missed incidents are surfaced.

capabilities.name: Role-based access and action permissions
capabilities.description: Can customers control who can view cases, change configuration, approve actions, and execute responses? Describe the permission granularity and separation of responsibilities.

capabilities.name: Documented APIs for customer integrations
capabilities.description: Which product functions and data are available through documented APIs? Explain how customers build integrations, including authentication, permissions, rate limits, and API versioning.

capabilities.name: Recorded decision rationale
capabilities.description: Does the product retain a reviewable explanation for each automated decision? Identify the inputs, rules or models used, and stated reasons recorded alongside the decision.

capabilities.name: Evidence-backed verdict and action explanations
capabilities.description: Can an analyst see why the product reached a verdict or chose an action? Explain how conclusions link to source evidence and how uncertainty or conflicting evidence is shown.

capabilities.name: Decision accuracy and error reporting
capabilities.description: Can customers measure correct and incorrect verdicts, missed incidents, and inconclusive results? Explain how outcomes are verified and whether the underlying data can be exported for independent review.

capabilities.name: Customer-provided AI models
capabilities.description: Can customers connect a model or model endpoint they control? Identify supported providers or hosting options, which functions can use them, and any limitations.

capabilities.name: Decisions grounded in customer context
capabilities.description: Which customer context informs decisions, such as past cases, asset criticality, identities, and business processes? Explain how it is gathered, kept current, and linked to the resulting conclusions.

capabilities.name: Granular autonomy limits and approval controls
capabilities.description: Can customers set what runs unattended and what needs approval by alert type, data source, severity, asset, or action? Cover automation, AI reasoning, and combinations of both, including overrides and emergency stops.

capabilities.name: Model quality monitoring and drift alerts
capabilities.description: How does the product detect declining accuracy or changes in model behavior over time? Explain what is monitored, how customers are notified, and how they can respond.

capabilities.name: Prompt injection and tool misuse testing
capabilities.description: How is the product tested against malicious instructions in alerts, retrieved content, or tool output? Describe protections against unsafe tool use and what test results customers can review.
